newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian customs seize Soros foundation money.
newsitem.headline: Croatian customs seize Soros foundation money.

text.p: Croatian customs on Thursday confiscated $65,000 from officials of a foundation formed by U.S. businessman George Soros, a week after president Franjo Tudjman brandished it as enemy of Croatia's independence.

State television said customs officials at Bregana border crossing with Slovenia found the money hidden in a private car with Zagreb plates, whose driver and co-driver were officials of Soros's Open Society.
"As they didn't report the money to the customs legal proceedings will be initiated and the sum will most probably be confiscated," the television said.
Zarko Puhovski, a prominent member of the foundation, told Reuters the driver, Srdjan Dvornik, was detained. Dvornik is Open Society's managing director.
The television claimed that a routine control had discovered a "secret channel for smuggling foreing currency into Croatia for financing Soros acitivities".
But a Finance Ministry official told Reuters that it was not necessary to report foreign currency upon entry.
Speaking at an annual congress of his nationalist HDZ party last Saturday, Tudjman said Soros' Open Society foundation had infiltrated the society, particularly culture and media.

He accused Soros, "other American and European foundations" and some Western embassies in Croatia of supporting the opposition, helping several small magazines and systematically enlarging the scope of their activities.
The foundation finances several media and cultural projects to promote democracy in Eastern Europe.

"With Soros's help they have infiltrated the entire society. They grant scholarships to all sorts of people and all generations... and they clearly state their aim is to change the ownership structure of the media," Tudjman said.
Open Society's deputy head Ivan Prpic said later he didn't expect further pressure or closure of the foundation.
Puhovski said the authorities were now taking the issue very seriously.
"It is difficult to say if the authorities will stop at this or if this will lead to further actions," he said.
